evidence.observation: start() is the legal idle->running lifecycle edge. It unconditionally resets session state, allocating a fresh threading.Event() as stop_event, clearing changed_files, and spawning a daemon thread running watch_files. Because it has no guard for an already-running watcher, a double start while running is an illegal edge that silently discards pending session changes.

stop() is the legal running->idle lifecycle edge. Both steps are guarded by 'if self.stop_event:' and 'if self.watcher_thread:', which makes stop() before start() and a repeated stop() safe no-ops rather than errors, and it resets both handles to None so the helper returns to a clean idle state.

handle_changes() rejects the empty/illegal change edge: an empty change list returns False without touching changed_files. A non-empty list is accepted, updates changed_files, calls io.interrupt_input(), and returns True, which is how pending watch work enters the session.

process_changes() is the command edge of the lifecycle: with an empty changed_files set it performs no work and returns the empty string, and it only derives an action ('!' or '?') from AI comments once changes are tracked, so no command is issued when the session has no pending watch work.

The existing watch test contract pins the legal/illegal handle_changes behaviour: handle_changes([]) is falsy and leaves changed_files empty, while a real change set returns truthy and records the path. The new lifecycle test extends this same helper contract to the start/stop state machine.

Shows the established test pattern in this repository for driving FileWatcher: a MinimalCoder with an InputOutput and a tmp_path root is passed to FileWatcher and observable methods are asserted directly, which the new lifecycle test follows with lighter stubs to avoid hard dependencies.

New executable state-transition test covering the legal edges: it asserts the watcher begins idle, that start() moves it to running with a fresh unset stop_event and empty changed_files, and that stop() returns it to idle with both handles set to None.

New executable state-transition test covering illegal edges: stop() before start() and a double stop() must be guarded no-ops that leave the watcher in the idle state rather than raising or producing an inconsistent handle pair.

New executable state-transition test for the unguarded illegal edge start() while already running: it demonstrates that pending changed_files are silently reset while the watcher remains running, then confirms stop() still returns it cleanly to idle.

New executable test for the change/command edges: handle_changes([]) returns False and is rejected, a real change set returns True and is tracked, and process_changes() with no pending work returns the empty string.

claims.claim: aider.watch.FileWatcher is a session/watch lifecycle helper with a two-state machine: legal edges idle--start()-->running and running--stop()-->idle, where start() installs a fresh stop_event plus daemon thread and stop() joins the thread and resets both handles to None.

The illegal lifecycle edges are guarded and benign: stop() before start() and a repeated stop() are no-ops because stop() checks 'if self.stop_event' and 'if self.watcher_thread', which the executable state-transition test verifies leaves the helper in the idle state.

start() is unguarded, so calling it while already running is an illegal edge that silently resets pending session state (changed_files cleared, new stop_event installed) while the watcher stays running; the state-transition test pins this behaviour.

handle_changes() rejects the empty change edge (returns False, state untouched) and accepts a non-empty change set (returns True and tracks it); tests/basic/test_watch.py already asserts this helper contract and the new lifecycle test reuses it as the work-intake edge of the state machine.
process_changes() is the command edge of the lifecycle: with no pending changed_files it emits no request and returns the empty string, so no command fires when the session has no watch work.

conclusion: The distinct session/watch/command lifecycle helper in aider is aider.watch.FileWatcher. Its start()/stop() pair forms a two-state machine (idle/running) that the new executable test tests/basic/test_watch_lifecycle.py exercises across legal edges (idle->start->running->stop->idle; non-empty change intake) and illegal edges (stop before start, double stop, double start, empty change set). The legal edges preserve the invariants that stop_event and watcher_thread move together and that a stopped watcher has both set to None; the guarded illegal edges are safe no-ops; and the single unguarded illegal edge (start() while running) is documented and pinned as silently resetting pending changed_files. Validation runs the four state-transition tests against the real FileWatcher methods and all pass.

validation.notes: All 4 state-transition tests passed (4 passed, 0 failed). LIMITATION: the offline environment does not have the optional third-party modules that aider/watch.py imports at load time ('watchfiles' and 'grep_ast'; 'oslex' is also absent for aider.io), and dependencies must not be installed. The harness .prale-eval/run_watch_lifecycle.py therefore registers minimal stub modules for watchfiles and grep_ast before loading tests/basic/test_watch_lifecycle.py, and the test replaces the OS watch loop with an event-driven loop (_LoopStubWatcher.watch_files) that is never the stub watchfiles.watch. The real FileWatcher.start/stop/handle_changes/process_changes implementations are exercised. In a fully provisioned environment the same tests run unchanged via 'python -m pytest tests/basic/test_watch_lifecycle.py'.
